findings.title: Deferred cancellation misses reminders due before the next cron run
findings.body: Booking cancellation now only marks scheduled emails as cancelled, while this job performs the SendGrid cancellation every 15 minutes. If a booking is cancelled five minutes before its reminder is due and the next cron run is ten minutes away, SendGrid still sends the reminder. The job then deletes the expired reminder at lines 34–41 before it can attempt cancellation. Reminders close to their send time need immediate cancellation rather than relying exclusively on the cron.

findings.title: Immediate reschedule cancellation retains the original SendGrid quota problem
findings.body: Rescheduling passes immediateDelete=true for every old email reminder, causing an immediate SendGrid cancellation even when the reminder is days away. These cancellations occupy the same 100 pending-cancellation slots that motivated this PR. Furthermore, the immediateDelete branch returns without marking the reminder cancelled, so if SendGrid rejects the request because the quota is full, the cron will never retry it. Repeated reschedules can therefore still cause old booking reminders to be sent; reschedules need the deferred cancellation/retry path as well.

findings.title: One failed cancellation prevents persistence of all preceding successes
findings.body: The Prisma delete calls are lazy promises accumulated until after every SendGrid request succeeds. If any request in the loop fails, execution jumps to the outer catch without executing any of those deletes, including deletes for batches successfully cancelled earlier. Those records are fetched again next run, and attempting to cancel an already cancelled batch can fail and repeatedly block later cancellations. Persist each successful cancellation before moving on and handle failures per reminder so one batch cannot prevent processing the rest.

findings.title: Await reminder cancellation updates before completing the request
findings.body: The cancellation helpers now perform the database deletion or cancelled=true update themselves, but their promises are discarded inside forEach and are not included in the awaited operations. Previously the database reminder deletions were collected and awaited. The handler can now return before these critical writes finish; on a serverless deployment execution can be suspended at that point, leaving reminders unmarked or unscheduled reminders still available to the scheduler. Collect and await the helper promises before responding.
